report.title: Vault Security Review
report.subject: src/Vault.sol
report.methodology: Manual line-by-line review, property enumeration, and adversarial scenario modelling against an over-collateralised single-asset lending vault.
report.note: This is an illustrative audit report produced for the Guardian Pipeline. It demonstrates how a static, point-in-time review (the artifact Landsman et al. 2025 found weakly correlated with exploit prevention) is converted into continuous, multi-layered assurance (Bourveau et al. 2024) by binding every security-relevant finding to a fuzz-harness invariant, a live monitor, and an exploit replay.

findings.title: Privileged attack() function can force protocol insolvency
findings.description: The attack() function, callable by the immutable `attacker` address, sets totalBorrowed = totalDeposited + 1 with no transfer or accounting basis. It exists solely to demonstrate live detection. A `block.chainid == BASE_MAINNET` backstop now reverts the call on Base mainnet, but it remains fully callable on testnets and local chains; while it executes, the vault is insolvent — liabilities exceed assets.
findings.recommendation: The mainnet chainid backstop (MainnetDisabled) is defence-in-depth, not a fix: remove attack() entirely before any production deployment. The function is retained in this codebase only as the controlled breach used by the Loom demo and the EXP-01 exploit replay.

continuousAssurance.rationale: A static review can flag attack() but cannot guarantee it is removed or that no equivalent privileged path is added later. INV-01/INV-07 are fuzz-proven pre-deploy and monitored every block, so any state where borrows exceed deposits is caught within one block regardless of the cause.

findings.title: Reentrancy exposure on state-mutating functions
findings.description: As raised: deposit, withdraw, borrow and repay performed ERC-20 transfers with no reentrancy protection — safe only while the asset is a standard non-callback ERC-20. A token with transfer hooks (ERC-777-style) would open a reentrancy surface against the liquidity and collateral checks. Remediation: the contract now inherits OpenZeppelin's ReentrancyGuard and all four mutating functions are marked `nonReentrant`, closing the reentrancy surface for any asset.
findings.recommendation: Resolved — retain the ReentrancyGuard. Note that the fuzz harness still exercises a non-callback MockERC20 and cannot reproduce a reentrant sequence, so INV-02 remains the continuous safety net for this class rather than the harness.

continuousAssurance.rationale: Although the ReentrancyGuard now blocks this class structurally, the fuzz harness exercises a non-callback MockERC20 and cannot reproduce a reentrant call sequence — so the finding is not proven absent by the harness. It is monitored live: any reentrancy that drained the liquidity buffer would break INV-02 and alert within one block. The traceability map surfaces this as monitored-only — a deliberately partial-coverage finding.

findings.title: sharePrice and collateralRatio are mutable storage with no setter
findings.description: sharePrice and collateralRatio are declared as mutable storage but the contract exposes no function to change them. They are effectively constants fixed at construction (1e18 and 8000 bps). A reader cannot tell from the type whether a future upgrade intends them to move, which obscures the security model around the share price floor.
findings.recommendation: Either mark the intent explicit (immutable / constant) or add governed setters with bounds. Until then, the fixed 1e18 sharePrice is the assumption the share-price-floor invariant protects.

continuousAssurance.rationale: INV-03 asserts sharePrice >= 1e18. If a future setter is added and ever drives the price below the peg, the harness fails pre-deploy and the live monitor alerts post-deploy — the finding stays covered even as the code evolves.

findings.title: Zero-share deposit possible if sharePrice ever exceeds the deposit amount
findings.description: deposit computes sharesMinted = amount * 1e18 / sharePrice with no `require(sharesMinted > 0)`. With the current fixed 1e18 sharePrice this is unreachable, but if sharePrice ever rises above `amount`, a depositor would increase totalDeposited while minting zero shares — donating funds to existing shareholders and desynchronising share accounting.
findings.recommendation: Add `require(sharesMinted > 0)` to deposit so a dust deposit at a high share price reverts rather than silently gifting value.

continuousAssurance.rationale: A zero-share deposit makes implied share value drift below deposits; INV-06 (no inflation) and INV-04 (share accounting) bound that drift. EXP-02 replays the ERC-4626 inflation class that this rounding latency belongs to.

findings.title: InsufficientLiquidity guards are provably unreachable at an 80% collateral ratio
findings.description: withdraw and borrow revert with InsufficientLiquidity when free liquidity cannot cover the requested amount. With collateralRatio fixed at 80%, free liquidity (totalDeposited - totalBorrowed >= 0.2*totalDeposited + 0.8*W) always covers any single user's withdrawable or borrowable value W, so the guards never trigger.
findings.recommendation: Keep the guards as defence-in-depth — they cost little and protect against a future collateralRatio change that would make them reachable. Document the unreachability proof so the dead branches are not mistaken for a coverage gap.

continuousAssurance.rationale: INV-02 is the property the unreachable guards exist to uphold. If a parameter change ever makes the guards reachable — or fails to — INV-02 still holds the line both in the harness and live. EXP-04 confirms the buffer survives a maximal borrow.

findings.title: Direct token donations desynchronise tokenBalance from accounting
findings.description: Anyone can transfer the asset directly to the vault, raising token.balanceOf(vault) above totalDeposited - totalBorrowed. This is benign for solvency (the balance only ever exceeds the requirement) but means tokenBalance is not a faithful proxy for protocol accounting, and a monitor naively equating the two would misreport.
findings.recommendation: Treat tokenBalance >= free liquidity as the correct relation (not equality). The Guardian evaluator already uses >=; no code change required.

continuousAssurance.rationale: INV-02 is intentionally a >= relation, so donations cannot break it. The harness and live monitor both encode the inequality, keeping the finding covered without a code change.

findings.title: collateralRatio could be immutable to save an SLOAD per borrow/withdraw
findings.description: collateralRatio is read on every borrow and withdraw from storage. As it is never written after construction it could be `immutable`, replacing the SLOAD with a code constant.
findings.recommendation: Mark collateralRatio immutable if no governed setter is planned.

continuousAssurance.rationale: This is a gas optimisation, not a security property. It is deliberately left out of the continuous-assurance map: the traceability tool excludes non-security-relevant findings from the coverage denominator so the metric is not inflated by unmonitorable items.

findings.title: No interest accrual leaves the vault unable to build a bad-debt reserve
findings.description: borrow and repay move principal only; there is no interest accrual, so sharePrice never rises and the protocol accumulates no reserve. Lenders earn nothing, and the vault has no buffer to absorb bad debt should a future change (e.g. a price oracle or liquidations) introduce undercollateralised positions.
findings.recommendation: If the vault is extended toward production, add an interest model and a reserve factor so the protocol can absorb shortfalls. Until then, solvency depends entirely on the collateral cap holding.

continuousAssurance.rationale: Without a reserve, the only thing standing between the vault and bad debt is solvency itself. INV-01/INV-07 are the continuous tripwire; EXP-03 replays the bad-debt class this finding warns about and confirms the collateral cap currently holds it off.
